model_interpretation.claim: The best measured candidate combines hoisted row bases with OpenMP SIMD (0.081288 s), while two no-directive candidates measured 0.449431 s and 0.461277 s. This experiment removes the SIMD directive but gives GCC/Clang a guarded no-alias guarantee for the coefficient, input, velocity, and output streams. The compiler may then auto-vectorize the contiguous-x loop without a target ISA, alignment, or fixed-width assumption; the ordinary loop still handles all widths and tails.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cpp"],"retained":["Removed the compile-gated OpenMP SIMD directive to test compiler auto-vectorization without an explicit SIMD hint.","Added GCC/Clang-guarded restrict qualifiers to the coefficient, stencil input, velocity, and output pointers to expose their non-aliasing relationship without asserting alignment or vector width.","Preserved the recurrence, initialization, boundaries, generic loop bounds, and scalar tail behavior."]}

model_interpretation.claim: The three prior OpenMP candidates are all valid and have similar aggregate means (0.2379–0.2416 s), but the supplied observations do not establish a clear per-thread comparison. This candidate tests persistent ownership of contiguous z-slabs across six steps, with five explicit dependency barriers and no per-step worksharing dispatch. Stable slab ownership may reduce scheduling overhead or improve locality; coarse slabs may limit utilization at small sizes. Controller measurements at one and four threads, including initialization, are needed before drawing a performance conclusion.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cpp"],"retained":["Replace the serial timestep sweep with one OpenMP team whose requested size is capped by the positive threads budget and the number of interior z-slices.","Partition interior z-slices into deterministic contiguous per-thread ranges, keeping each thread on its slab for all six steps while traversing contiguous x positions.","Select input/output buffers by timestep parity and place an explicit barrier between dependent timesteps; rely on the parallel-region completion for the final step.","Preserve full initialization of both output buffers, the original stencil arithmetic, update bounds, and unchanged boundary behavior."]}

items.subject: Combiner l’auto-vectorisation avec le parallélisme persistant
items.objective: Combiner le candidat T2 d96 (bases de lignes, sans directive SIMD, avec restrict pour l’aliasing) au parallélisme persistant par lignes de T1, en partant de d96. Évaluer la combinaison à un et quatre cœurs contre Gm1 et ses parents, sans présumer que leurs gains s’additionnent; préserver la correction et les contraintes du protocole.
